extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy; philosophers and scholars of metaphysics
extracted.subtask_short: metaphysical essay on matter and will
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a philosophical treatise arguing that 'matter' is the visibility/objectification of the will and assessing materialism, atomism, determinism, and the proper starting-points for metaphysics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy must start from absolutely immediate self-consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy necessarily requires what is absolutely immediate for its starting-point; only that which is given in self-consciousness fulfils this condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subjective (self-consciousness) is the only absolute immediate datum; therefore Descartes' move to begin with self-consciousness is meritorious. Genuine philosophy proceeds by analysing self-consciousness (idea and will) rather than beginning from external perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise two immediate data: idea and will
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two completely different data of immediate knowledge in self-consciousness — the idea and the will — whose combined application advances philosophy further than either alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both the idea (objective/representational aspect) and the will (subjective inner nature) as foundational data; their joint use permits deeper metaphysical conclusions than starting from one alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid petitio principii in metaphysical systems (critique of materialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materialism's primary error is assuming matter to be absolutely and unconditionally given, i.e., treating matter as a thing in itself — a petitio principii.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid metaphysical system must not presuppose as given the very thing it must explain. Materialism illicitly takes its Quæsita (what should be explained) as Data, leading to illegitimate conclusions (e.g., hidden assumptions of forces) and failing as ultimate explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physics/naturalism cannot serve as ultimate metaphysics
rubrics_metrics.description: Physics and naturalism begin after many assumptions and therefore cannot claim to give the ultimate explanation of things; they leave qualitate occultae and other primitives unexplained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because physical science presupposes forms (space, time, causality) and many empirical forces, it cannot replace metaphysics; ultimate philosophical explanation must address the immediate subjective grounds rather than rely on empirical science alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matter is the visibility/objectivity of the will
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter is simply the visibility of the will; as thing-in-itself the will becomes objective and appears as matter (phenomenon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat matter not as an independently existing thing-in-itself but as the objectified form in which the will appears. Consequences: matter in itself is incorporeal (no extension), empirical properties (e.g., gravity) are manifestations/grades of the will, and one cannot think matter without the forms imposed by the intellect (space, time, causality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reduce qualitative properties to purely quantitative/mechanical explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is illegitimate to refer all qualitative phenomena to mere quantitative 'form' and thereby reduce vital and other original forces to mechanical activity of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware arguments that collapse qualities into quantities (e.g., reducing life to chemistry, or all forces to molecular/atomic mechanics) without justification. Such reductions conceal unexplained 'qualitates occultae' and result in unsupported atomistic fictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of atomism and unjustified mechanical analogies
rubrics_metrics.description: Atomism and hypotheses like vibrating ether are chimerical and rest on arbitrary analogies (e.g., with music); they offer implausible, ad hoc constructions rather than genuine explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand empirical and conceptual adequacy for mechanical hypotheses. The text cites the implausibility of assuming countless independent ether-oscillations and uses experimental puzzles (e.g., chemical effects of light) to challenge simplistic mechanical models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciling determinism and freedom by assigning necessity to action and freedom to being
rubrics_metrics.description: While the law of causality makes all action strictly necessitated (determinism), the thing-in-itself (will) can be conceived as absolutely free; thus freedom should be placed in the 'being' (Esse) and necessity in the 'acting' (Operari).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A coherent metaphysical view must accept empirical determinism of actions (character + motives) yet preserve transcendental freedom of the will by distinguishing existence/nature (free) from observable conduct (necessitated). This resolves the apparent contradiction without denying causal law.
